notes: Coverage: I read the whole image once for layout, then half_a once and half_b once in that order, comparing every text block and every word, ending, accent, abbreviation, punctuation mark, insertion, deletion and inline formula with both C and H. There are no separate displays, diagrams, non-diagram drawings, headings, date, salutation, signature or author page number on this page. No other page image, other reader folder, OCR, PDF text layer or external source was used.

The page is wholly handwritten. Its main hand is not independently identified by this packet, so it is recorded conservatively as an unnamed hand. The bottom-left 10 is an archive number, preserved as the required comment; H’s page{10} already carries that metadata and is not counted as an omission.

All twelve crops are tight open-locus crops from the whole-source raster, generated once each and inspected once. c11 resolved an agreed spelling rather than creating a change row. c04 also revealed the separate high point above its neighbouring comma; c09 distinguishes the prime from the top of the following parenthesis. No whole or half image was reopened for visual inspection. Source images were loaded computationally only to read dimensions and generate the listed crops.

For differences settled in the halves, approximate whole-source boxes are retained in each change entry’s observation field. The retained coordinates do not represent a later image view. The main reader still needs personal adjudication views for those differences. Crop c06 incidentally includes the already settled tte abbreviation as context for the unresolved cancellation.

H’s editorial note correctly credits the interlinear s’obtient en and L and the opening replacement; macro conversions alone are not differences. Its external statement about another exemplar was not used as evidence. The source insertion hooks are represented by inserted at the relevant attachments, not as separate drawings.

The prose says, with the explicit qualification sauf erreur, that every homomorphism M to left-subscript-2 N comes from a suitable Picard champ. It places an obstruction in Ext^3(X;M,N) and says a universel argument proves it null. These are statements made by the page, not proof checks performed in this run.

The page then says the extension alpha is close to splitting: every section over an object of X lifts, giving an ensembliste section; it adds a claim of origin in a degree-two hypercohomology group. The actual verb is remonte. The abbreviation tte and comma after alpha are retained.

The first adjective is too faded to decide whether the low internal mark is a dash or a worn n. The later occurrence épinglé has an observable shoulder after i. No reading from the prior notation snapshot overrides either form.

The script-H font choice is not presented as a mathematical distinction proved here: both TeX script alphabets approximate the two-loop pen form. The physical separation of the right-edge high point and low comma-like mark prevents reducing them to a single comma/full-stop choice. The phantom alternatives deny a textual character, not the existence of the physical marks.
No mathematical proof, computation or formal structural test was attempted. The mathematical work in this return is visual transcription only. No LaTeX compilation was run.
